question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{4},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{{x}^{6}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{5}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{5}{3{x}^{3}}|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-{(\frac{5}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{48}.\end{aligned}
$$
